payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source DVD visibly transformed to white in EDITED?
node.criteria: Judge whether the DVD shown in SOURCE is visibly white rather than black in EDITED. A white disc or other DVD-like object alone does not establish this endpoint; the edited candidate must be supported as the same source object by its location, shape, or visible features. Preserve uncertainty if correspondence cannot be established.
node.binding: Compare the small rectangular, image-bearing DVD case near the center of SOURCE with plausible objects in EDITED, using location, shape, and visible features to assess continuity before judging color. Do not treat a nearby white disc as the transformed DVD solely because it is white or DVD-like.
node.source_quote: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
node.endpoint: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
node.necessity: Changing the DVD’s color to white is the explicit requested transformation.
node.zero_when: The source DVD remains black, no requested color change is visible on an object supported as that DVD, or only an unrelated/new white disc is visible.
node.half_when: Evidence supports that an edited candidate is the source DVD and it shows a concrete but incomplete change toward white, with substantial black coloration remaining; unresolved correspondence alone is not evidence of partial color fulfillment.
node.full_when: The source DVD is supported as the same object in EDITED by its location, shape, or visible features, and that object is visibly white rather than black, allowing natural lighting, texture, and photographic variation.

node_traces.evidence: The source DVD is the small rectangular, image-bearing case near the center. In EDITED, that object is not visibly present at its source location; instead, there are two white circular discs, one near the center and one beside the dark object on the right. Neither is supported by the source DVD’s rectangular shape or visible features as the same object. The white discs therefore do not establish the requested transformation.

d2: The binding is too vague about which source object is the target: the source shows a small rectangular DVD case near the center, while the edited image has two white circular discs, one near the center-left and one over the dark object. Avoid treating “recognizable as a DVD” as evidence of identity or assuming either disc is the transformed case. Make the comparison explicitly track the source target’s location, shape, and continuity into the edited image, and distinguish a changed target from newly appearing or unrelated objects. The trace’s high-confidence partial judgment reflects ambiguity, not proof of partial requested progress; assess whether any visible change can be attributed to the bound target, and keep unresolved identity distinct from confirmed progress. The reference label alone does not establish that the target is absent.
